line.name: Twentieth Anniversary
line.wrapper: Honduran (sun-grown; offered in natural and Maduro wrapper options)
line.background_text: Released in 2015 to commemorate Rocky Patel's 20th year in the cigar industry (founded 1995), this line kept most of its blend recipe a closely guarded 'trade secret,' disclosing only the regional origins of the tobacco. It launched with a box-pressed Toro as the flagship vitola plus several companion sizes including a Lancero and Rothschild, and was marketed heavily around a pre-release 90-point rating.

vitolas.summary_review: Halfwheel scored the Rothschild 91, praising orange peel, meatiness and peanut notes early, developing into French onion soup, salty popcorn, bourbon and smoky oak.

critic_reviews.key_notes_text: Halfwheel scored the Rothschild 91, describing a complex progression from orange peel and peanuts to French onion soup, bourbon and smoky oak.

vitolas.summary_review: CigarScore.com rated the box-pressed Toro poorly (2/10) citing burn issues and inconsistent flavor delivery despite a promising, short-lived butterscotch note.

critic_reviews.key_notes_text: CigarScore.com rated the box-pressed Toro low (2/10), citing burn problems and an inconsistent, though occasionally good, flavor profile.

vitolas.summary_review: Leaf Enthusiast scored the Lancero an exceptional 9.5/10, calling it 'easily the best Rocky Patel product' the reviewer had smoked, citing cherry, cedar, coffee, earth, leather and pepper spice.

critic_reviews.key_notes_text: Leaf Enthusiast scored the Lancero 9.5/10, calling it the best Rocky Patel product the reviewer had tried, with sweet cherry, cedar, coffee, earth, leather and pepper spice.

research_notes: Confirmed distinct from 'Rocky Patel Vintage 20th Anniversary' (a separate extension of the older Vintage 1990 line, using Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper/Brazilian binder) -- the two are different products despite similar naming. Robusto Grande's length/ring gauge could not be confirmed in available sources.
